d: Russia’s push to replace the US dollar with China’s yuan is faltering, with the yuan’s share of Russian export payments halving to 22% amid sanctions, Chinese banks’ reluctance and Beijing’s capital controls. Meanwhile, Iran has threatened to strike Europe if NATO nations allow Donald Trump to use their airbases for renewed attacks on Tehran. With Iranian ballistic and cruise missiles potentially capable of reaching parts of Europe, the threats raise fears of a wider conflict. Is Moscow losing faith in the yuan, and could Tehran’s warning drag Europe into another confrontation? Hem Kaur…
